summary: Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held positions at Rissho University (professor attested 2001, professor emeritus attested 2026) and the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, he taught at Osaka University (1964–1968), Hokkaido University (professor 1968–1991, emeritus attested 1986–1997), and Sapporo Otani Junior College.
Kotetsu Yoshida is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as professor emeritus at Taisho University and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute, both attested in 2014.
Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and later held a post at Taisho University.

Koun Yamada (1907–1989) was a Buddhist and religious studies master educated at First Higher School. He studied under teachers including Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, whom he succeeded from 1961 to 1989, and founded the Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953.

Koyo Sakaino (1871–1933) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held academic posts at Toyo University (ca. 1904–1923) and Komazawa University.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) studied at the University of Tokyo and worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served at Nishogakusha University, the Department of Cultural Affairs, and Toyo University (associate professor 1972, professor emeritus 1977–2000).

Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin, and founded Shakuson Shofukai in 1893.

Kozui Otani (1876–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist, Iranian, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Gakushuin and Kyoritsu Gakusha under Keiun Maeda, he served as the 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914) and founded Kojukai in 1919.
Kripa Shankar Shukla (1918–2007) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who held posts at the University of Lucknow until 1959 and as attested in 1976.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University. He held academic posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indologist educated at Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. Educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College, Kolkata, he later taught at Hare School (ca. 1829–1832) and Bishop's College (1852).

Indologist K. V. Sarma (1919–2005) studied at University College Thiruvananthapuram and University of Kerala. He held posts at ORI & Manuscripts Library, University of Madras, Panjab University, VVRI, and Adyar Library, and founded the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi (1918–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Bangalore University, Honorary Director of the Dvaita Vedanta Studies and Research Foundation, and Upakulapati at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha (attested 1997).

Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology scholar who studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is an Indology and linguistics scholar affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient and an editorial board member of Studies on the History of Śaivism, both attested in 2021.

Kristin Johnston Largen works in religious and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at Wartburg Theological Seminary, United Lutheran Seminary as Professor of Systematic Theology (attested 2018), and Gettysburg College (attested 2018).

Kristin Scheible is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Colby College and Harvard University under Anne E. Monius and Diana L. Eck. She has taught at Harvard, Brown, Bard College, and Reed College.
